claims.statement: The Node API controls instance configuration, data and runtime resources; Portal manages accounts, subscriptions and JWTs; Management Studio is the selected subscription's configuration/administration UI, not an interchangeable backend API.

Node paths such as /pipes are relative to the instance API base ending in /api; Portal paths already include /api except explicit /.well-known/openid-configuration; DAP paths are relative to the DAP host. All three local Swagger files declare Swagger 2.0/version 0.0.0 without basePath.

Service API renders checked-in Node and Portal Swagger copies and separately points to running references at the instance /api/reference and https://portal.sesam.io/api/reference; narrative examples are not additional Swagger operations.

The narrative instance POST /api/jwt example has no /jwt operation in Node Swagger; email/password JWT issuance is specified in Portal POST /api/jwt, leaving deployment-specific instance routing unproven here.

Node Swagger includes routes with api.view_utils._not_in_use_ IDs and sparse schemas such as Pump; those identifiers and omitted media types/error tables do not establish route unavailability or complete runtime failure behavior.

Portal roles are subscription-scoped; Portal signs JWTs carrying those roles, Node verifies with the Portal public key and checks resource ACL permissions, and denied dataset reads return 403 Forbidden.
New pipes inherit creator roles in configuration; runtime source-read/target-write permission checks can fail the run and display an error on its UI page.

GET/PUT /config select the default group, /config/{config-group} one tagged group, and /config-all all groups; PUT replaces the entire scope. GET returns ConfigEntity arrays or ZIP; uploads consume JSON, ZIP or multipart/form-data, with 200 responses.

Individual pipe/system grouping uses metadata.$config-group and defaults to default, while bulk grouping selects the group in the URL; Swagger calls the default group 'default (i.e empty)' and the narrative names it default.

Configuration force defaults false where declared and true accepts errors for best-effort application; group GET declares force but group PUT does not, and /config and /config-all descriptions spell header selection 'Accepts'.
GET /config-history/entity requires entity_id and returns JSON ConfigEntity history with optional limit (unset means all), opaque integer since, and reverse=false.
GET/PUT/DELETE /metadata return JSON ServiceMetadata arrays at 200; DELETE removes all service metadata and PUT has no declared body schema.

GET /pipes returns JSON Pipe arrays with verbose=false and optional fields config/runtime/storage/graph; POST takes required PipeConfig arrays with force=false and returns new Pipe arrays; GET/DELETE /pipes/{pipe_id} read/delete individual pipes with 200.
GET /pipes/{pipe_id}/config returns JSON PipeConfig; PUT requires PipeConfig with force=false and returns JSON Pipe at 200, without a declared request media type.

Pipe responses distinguish original config from effective config after environment-variable/shorthand expansion and expose runtime validity/errors; PipeConfigError supplies elements JSON path, level error/warning, and msg.
Multinode aggregators can return cached subnode information when a subnode is unresponsive, marking items with cached_response_info containing timestamp and age in seconds.

GET /pipes/{pipe_id}/pump returns JSON Pump; POST consumes form-urlencoded or multipart with required operation and returns JSON Pump at 200. Operations are capability-dependent; the narrative advises consulting runtime.supported-operations.

Pump start manually starts a run; enable permits automatic runs; disable prevents automatic scheduling but permits manual starts and lets current runs finish; stop stops normal/rescan runs or does nothing when idle.
update-last-seen accepts source-specific string last-seen and empty string clears continuation; set-last-seen-to-end is source-dependent and can lose data by skipping unread entities.
start-rescan starts unless already running; reset-rescan makes the next scan start at the beginning rather than resume an interrupted scan.

Experimental reset-tracking is unsafe while running and resumes tracking at dependent dataset ends when the next pump runs, skipping offsets and potentially producing incorrect output; intended for development or followed by full sync.
discard-retries records pump-discard-retries so pending write-error retries are ignored on the next run; discarded entities are not written to dead-letter storage.
discard-inferred-schema removes accumulated schema and normally should be followed by reset, particularly for pipes without continuation that do not automatically delete schema on reset.
Disable can persist a comment in the pump-disabled execution-log entity; dont-wait-for-pump-to-start and relation are deprecated form parameters for older versions/operations.

Management Studio Restart is reset plus start, Reset reprocesses from the beginning, and Delete sink dataset removes the sink dataset and resets since; these UI workflows do not introduce similarly named pump operation strings.

GET /pipes/{pipe_id}/entities returns JSON PipeEntity arrays with optional unbounded limit, string since, and stage=sink or source/before-transforms/after-transforms; generate-schema-definition GET returns JSON with sample_size and keys_only=false.

GET /pipes/{pipe_id}/log returns JSON DatasetEntity arrays with limit, opaque integer since, history=true, reverse=false, deleted=true and full-history deletes always included; OPTIONS returns text/plain and supports experimental webhook plus associated token or Badrequest.
POST /pipes/{pipe_id}/webhook consumes JSON with the registered token and schedules a pump; unknown/mismatched webhook or pipe returns 404, documented as unregistering the webhook on the sender side.

GET /datasets returns JSON Dataset arrays with verbose=false; individual GET/DELETE inspect/delete a dataset; POST /datasets/{dataset_id} is a form rollback-circuit-breaker or commit-circuit-breaker operation, not ingestion, with JSON/200 responses.

GET /datasets/{dataset_id}/entities returns JSON DatasetEntity arrays with unbounded limit when absent, opaque integer since, history=true, reverse=false and deleted=true; history=false selects latest versions and full history always includes replaced versions/deletes.

Dataset-list populated=true adds 404 until a complete populated source view exists; unknown JSON-encoded subset gives 404; uncommitted=true can expose circuit-breaker-uncommitted data for debugging. Boolean controls default false.

GET /datasets/{dataset_id}/entity requires entity_id and supports subset, offset, uncommitted=false; unknown subset or absent/mismatched entity at offset gives 404. /entities/{rest_of_path} is deprecated in favor of /entity; DatasetEntity._updated is the integer offset.

OPTIONS /datasets/{dataset_id}/entities returns text/plain and supports since/history/reverse/deleted/subset plus experimental webhook and required token; missing token gives Badrequest and new data triggers a webhook POST after request processing.
Dataset inspection GET /datasets/{dataset_id}/indexes returns JSON DatasetIndex arrays; GET generate-schema-definition uses sample_size and keys_only=false and returns JSON, both 200.
Dataset SDShare collection/feed GETs return application/atom+xml; GET /datasets/{dataset_id}/sdshare-fragments/{rest_of_path} returns application/n-triples for an entity, all 200.
Service API explicitly prohibits production dataset-API writes and directs ingestion to an HTTP endpoint source or JSON Push, despite Swagger including POST /datasets/{dataset_id}/entities.
Dataset entity POST consumes/produces JSON with 200; force=false suppresses equal-hash writes while force=true always writes, unlike configuration force accepting errors.
http_endpoint sources register receiver URLs without a pump; entities flow through their pipe to the sink only when posted.

POST /receivers/{pipe_id}/entities is JSON Push for an http_endpoint pipe, consuming/producing JSON with a 200 object and optional Swagger query controls sequence_id, request_id, previous_request_id, is_full (described default false), is_first and is_last.

JSON Push specifies an array even for one entity while the HTTP endpoint narrative permits single objects; full sync has one active sequence, a new full sequence replaces it and is_last closes it, whereas incremental requests do not affect it.

Full-sync previous-request mismatch, inconsistent is_full, or invalid repeated is_first require 409 Conflict; the sink stops/retries later, restarting full sync with a new sequence from the beginning. Incremental controls may be ignored; these are narrative failure rules beyond Swagger's 200 table.

With dataset enable_optimistic_locking, the receiver may return updated_entity for a one-entity post or input_entity/existing_entity/common_ancestor_entity for stale _updated input and three-way merge, as fields in its 200 schema rather than a distinct status table.

SDShare receiver POST requires an http_endpoint source and N-Triples body, consumes application/n-triples or text/plain and returns text/plain/200. resource is optional in Swagger but required in source narrative; no statements for a resource yields _deleted=true, graph is ignored and sink determines destination.

Publisher GETs expose entities JSON, CSV text/csv, Excel application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, XML application/xml, and SDShare feeds application/atom+xml; since/unbounded limit apply except SDShare collection, filename variants set attachment names, and CSV linked_excel_file returns an Excel connection file instead of CSV.
Office publisher OPTIONS paths preserve trailing slashes at /publishers/{pipe_id}/csv/, /excel/, /xml/, with text/plain/200 responses.
Shareable links use GET/POST /publishers/{pipe_id}/shareable-links returning JSON ShareableLink arrays/record and individual DELETE; POST requires NewShareableLink and all declare 200.

Systems provide list GET verbose=false with verbose disk-usage storage breakdown, POST required SystemConfig arrays and force=false, individual GET/DELETE and config GET/PUT; config PUT requires and returns SystemConfig rather than pipe PUT's Pipe, at 200.

GET /systems/{system_id}/logs defaults to 1000 lines and ISO datetime since selects all later lines; status GET returns system status/Docker inspect subset for microservices, both 200 without declared media type/schema.
POST /systems/{system_id}/reload asynchronously queues image pull and microservice recreation and returns 202 rather than completed reload confirmation.
GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE system proxy operations pass requests to required microservice-relative rest_of_path and return proxied responses with 200 but no fixed media types/body schema.

Global GET /secrets lists names; PUT/POST use JSON name-to-value payloads overwriting matching values and POST retains others; DELETE removes named secret. Responses declare JSON/200 without consumes declarations.

System secret GET lists SecretKeys, PUT overwrites secrets, POST adds/overwrites supplied values while retaining others, and individual DELETE removes one; bodies use SecretValues mapping and responses JSON/200.
Secrets are strongly encrypted with an instance-unique key and unrecoverable in original form after upload, requiring secure off-site storage.
Global secrets last until explicit deletion; system secrets also disappear with system removal, requiring re-upload after deleting/re-adding a system.
$SECRET(key) substitution applies only to System configuration and resolves as needed at runtime without exposing values in API/logs.
Node health GET returns JSON 200 or unhealthy 503, ping GET returns JSON 200, and root GET returns JSON status with aggregated=true unless false is requested.

Narrative /api/metrics is a Prometheus-compatible scrape requiring Metrics and monitoring enabled on a clustered subscription and an Admin JWT; Node Swagger has no /metrics operation. Pump metrics are absent for disabled/manual/off pipes.

Portal standard subscription/pipe monitoring GETs return JSON standard monitoring information at 200; /api/monitoring/invoicing/{subscription_id} returns invoicing information rather than Prometheus metrics.

Portal root GET returns JSON status/feature-level and authentication providers; login POST consumes form email/password plus optional captcha and creates a session cookie; signup POST consumes required globally unique email/password/name plus optional captcha, returning JSON/200.

Portal profile GET returns Profile; PUT accepts userInfo/profile sparse updates preserving missing fields and cannot change email; profile2 GET adds 401 when unauthenticated with replacement only a TODO; individual profile DELETE deletes the user.
Portal logout GET is deprecated legacy logout returning Profile at 200; logout2 clears session and redirects 302 to Portal or third-party logout.

Portal password PUT requires password/old_password; forgot-password POST emails a one-time link; reset-password POST requires password/token. Form operations return 200 objects requiring boolean success, with reset response media type undeclared.
Portal verify-emailaddress POST requires token and returns 400 for invalid/used/expired tokens or 200 on success; request-email-verification POST returns 409 if mail is pending, otherwise 200.
Portal provider login POST and login_callback GET use 302 redirects; implicit-flow GET serves HTML extracting fragment id_token and calling POST /api/jwt_login.

Portal subscription CRUD uses collection GET/POST and individual GET/PUT/DELETE, optional NewSubscriptionInfo creation body and required UpdatedSubscriptionInfo update body, with JSON Subscription arrays/records and 200 responses.

Portal available-roles GET/POST lists built-in/custom roles and creates custom RoleInfo; individual GET/PUT/DELETE reads/updates/deletes RoleInfo at JSON/200, managing subscription roles rather than Node ACLs.

Portal members GET uses start=0 and optional unbounded limit returning SubscriptionMemberInfo arrays; POST invites with InvitedUser; individual GET/PUT reads/updates roles with UpdatedSubscriptionMemberInfo, all JSON/200.

Portal JWT GETs return current-user tokens as text/plain; POST /api/jwt takes form email/password and optional subscription_id defaulting to all user subscriptions; publickey GET returns RSA verification key as text/plain, all 200.

Portal API JWT records use collection GET/POST/PUT and individual DELETE; creation requires jwt_settings exp/principals for script/cron tokens; update requires a body but no individual schema-required settings. Responses are JSON SubscriptionJWT arrays/records or OK at 200.

API JWT exp is seconds since Epoch; refresh_interval makes it the final refreshable time while signed expiry is current time plus interval. jwt_string/client_secret return only at creation; api_token_id supports Node invalidation checks and principals maps one subscription to its principals.

Portal discovery GET returns JSON provider configuration; token POST consumes form grant_type client_credentials/refresh_token, client_id/client_secret and returns JSON/200 without detailed response/error fields.
Databrowser end-of-life is documented as December 31, 2023 with Integrated Search its successor; DAP Swagger explicitly restricts endpoints to internal use subject to arbitrary change/removal.

Legacy DAP config uses higher-numbered layers over lower ones, with /sesam/data base applied last over numbered layers and /sesam/conf; Swagger and narrative curl use /configuration/conf/{config_layer}/{config_file_path} while the narrative introduction omits conf.

DAP file GET returns text/plain or octet-stream/200 with empty body for absent files; PUT/DELETE return JSON with errors possible at 200 and 403 to prevent lockout. validate_only defaults false and true validates without changes; errors cover the full config set and response requires validity/lockout/error fields.

Historical DAP file APIs require JWT-enabled configuration and Admin JWT; configuration GET serves embeddable HTML via content_only, and config_file_path is an explicitly imperfect Swagger rest-of-path representation not to be URL-escaped.

Connector tools document manifest-based system/pipe generation, expand on sesam upload, collapse after download, automatic OAuth 2.0 authorization or sesam authenticate, and link an external client README rather than define new Swagger operations.

Configuration tests use expected result/.test.json files per endpoint pipe, drain queues with outbound systems disabled/unreachable and compare using sesam -vv test; default reads use pipe entities at sink stage and publisher tests can use configured endpoints/bound parameters.

CI testing requires a designated node and serial tests because uploads overwrite config, with outbound access disabled and necessary outbound secrets/variables absent; Sesam Client forbids production use, simultaneous clients on a subscription, and concurrent manual edits.
